description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic known for its succulent chicken pieces simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based gravy. This iconic dish offers a perfect balance of tangy, sweet, and mildly spiced flavors, making it a comforting and utterly delicious meal. Prepare to be enchanted by its velvety texture and aromatic appeal, a true taste of Indian culinary heritage.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, Kashmiri red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon oil in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until lightly browned and slightly charred. The chicken does not need to be fully cooked through at this stage. Remove the chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add 1 tablespoon butter. Once melted, add the green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Saute for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until aromatic.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews, remaining 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon salt to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the mixture has thickened. Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods if desired for a smoother gravy.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender. Add 1/2 cup water or chicken broth. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken pieces to the smooth gravy. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, heavy cream, and honey or sugar. Stir gently to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over low heat and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to finish cooking through. Crush the dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) between your palms and stir them into the butter chicken. Adjust seasoning if needed.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve the Classic Butter Chicken hot with basmati rice, naan bread, or roti. Enjoy this rich and flavorful Indian delicacy!

tips: For an authentic flavor, do not skip the kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves); crush them between your palms before adding to release their aroma. This is key to traditional Butter Chicken.

Achieve the signature rich color without excessive spice by using Kashmiri red chili powder, which provides vibrant color with mild heat. Adjust sugar/honey and cream to balance the tanginess of tomatoes to your preference.
Butter Chicken tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld further. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 2-3 months.
article:
Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani, holds a revered place in the pantheon of Indian cuisine. This globally beloved dish is a symphony of tender chicken pieces swimming in a rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato-based sauce. Its unparalleled popularity stems from its comforting texture and balanced flavors, making it a universal favorite, from bustling Indian kitchens to fine dining establishments across the world. If you’ve ever craved a dish that embodies warmth, luxury, and authentic Indian taste, then classic Butter Chicken is undoubtedly the answer.

Originating from the culinary genius of the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s, Butter Chicken was born out of a need to utilize leftover tandoori chicken. The chefs simmered the chicken in a luscious tomato and butter gravy, creating a dish that quickly captivated palates and etched itself into culinary history. Today, we’ll explore the essence of this iconic recipe, guiding you through its preparation to recreate that authentic, restaurant-quality taste in your own home.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

The story of Butter Chicken begins in post-partition India, specifically in Delhi, where Kundan Lal Jaggi and Kundan Lal Gujral, founders of Moti Mahal, innovated this dish. Murgh Makhani literally translates to "chicken with butter," a name that perfectly encapsulates its core ingredients and luxurious feel. It’s characterized by a vibrant orange-red sauce that is incredibly smooth, thanks to puréed tomatoes and often, ground cashews or cream. The chicken, traditionally tandoori-cooked, is marinated in yogurt and spices before being grilled or pan-fried, ensuring it remains incredibly tender and flavorful.

Unlike some spicier Indian curries, Butter Chicken is known for its mild, subtly sweet, and tangy profile, achieved through a careful balance of tomatoes, butter, cream, and aromatic spices like garam masala, fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), and a touch of sugar. This harmonious blend makes it approachable for all palates, including those new to Indian food, solidifying its status as a gateway dish to the diverse and flavorful world of Indian cuisine.

## Ingredients for Classic Butter Chicken

To create the perfect Butter Chicken, you’ll need fresh, high-quality ingredients. This recipe focuses on achieving that authentic taste profile.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   1 kg boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1.5-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt

For the Makhani (Butter) Sauce:
*   4 tablespoons unsalted butter (plus more for finishing)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1.5 cups tomato purée (from canned crushed tomatoes or fresh blended tomatoes)
*   1/2 cup cashew paste (soak 1/4 cup cashews in hot water for 30 mins, then blend with a little water) OR 1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances tanginess)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth (as needed for consistency)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, for finishing
*   Salt to taste

Garnish:
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped
*   A swirl of fresh cream

## How to Make Butter Chicken: Step-by-Step

The journey to delicious Butter Chicken involves a few key stages, each contributing to the final masterpiece.

Step 1: Marinate the Chicken
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.

Step 2: Cook the Chicken
Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F) or heat a grill pan/skillet over medium-high heat. Skewer the marinated chicken pieces (if grilling) or arrange them on a baking sheet. Cook for 15-20 minutes in the oven, turning once, until cooked through and slightly charred at the edges. If using a skillet, cook in batches for about 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked. Set aside.

Step 3: Prepare the Sauce Base
In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

Step 4: Build the Flavor
Stir in the tomato purée, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Cook, stirring frequently, for 10-15 minutes, allowing the tomatoes to break down and the spices to cook through. The sauce should deepen in color and start to release oil.

Step 5: Blend for Smoothness
Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot). Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silken texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot.

Step 6: Finish the Makhani Sauce
Return the pot to low-medium heat. Stir in the cashew paste (or the first 1/2 cup of heavy cream if using instead of cashews), kasoori methi, sugar, and salt to taste. Add 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth to achieve your desired consistency; the sauce should be thick but pourable. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Step 7: Combine and Serve
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering sauce. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors of the sauce. Just before serving, stir in the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter and the final 1/2 cup of heavy cream. Heat through gently without boiling.

Garnish with fresh cilantro and a swirl of cream.

## Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Mastering the art of Butter Chicken involves a few crucial tips that elevate it from good to extraordinary:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't rush the marination process. Longer marination (4+ hours) ensures incredibly tender and flavorful chicken.
*   **Quality Butter:** Use good quality unsalted butter. It's a key ingredient, and its flavor will shine through.
*   **Smooth Sauce:** Blending the sauce until absolutely smooth is crucial for the classic restaurant-style texture. Don't skip this step.
*   **Kasoori Methi is Essential:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) impart a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is quintessential to Butter Chicken. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their oils.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste and adjust. The sauce should be a balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy. A pinch of sugar can cut the acidity of tomatoes, and a squeeze of lemon juice can brighten the flavors.
*   **Don't Overcook Chicken:** Once the chicken is added to the sauce, simmer just long enough for the flavors to meld. Overcooking will make the chicken tough.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

Serving your homemade Butter Chicken is as delightful as making it. This rich curry pairs perfectly with a variety of Indian breads and rice dishes.

*   **Indian Breads:** Warm, fluffy naan bread (garlic naan is a fantastic choice!), roti, or paratha are perfect for scooping up every last bit of the luscious sauce.
*   **Rice:** Basmati rice, plain steamed rice, or fragrant jeera (cumin) rice make excellent accompaniments, soaking up the creamy gravy beautifully.
*   **Accompaniments:** A side of cooling cucumber raita (yogurt dip), a simple kachumber salad (diced onion, tomato, cucumber), or mango chutney can provide a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry.

## Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is divine, don't hesitate to experiment with variations to suit your dietary needs or preferences.

*   **Healthier Version:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream. You can substitute some of the cream with Greek yogurt (added off the heat to prevent curdling) or skip cashews and use a touch more tomato.
*   **Spicier Kick:** For those who prefer more heat, increase the red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili along with the ginger-garlic paste.
*   **Vegetarian Butter "Chicken":** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) for Paneer Makhani, or use firm tofu, mushrooms, or mixed vegetables for a delicious vegetarian alternative.
*   **Nut-Free Option:** If you have a nut allergy, omit the cashews and increase the heavy cream slightly, or use sunflower seeds as a thickener.
*   **Dairy-Free:** Substitute butter with a plant-based oil or vegan butter, and use full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream instead of dairy cream and yogurt.

Butter Chicken is more than just a dish; it's an experience. Its creamy texture, tender chicken, and perfectly balanced spices offer a taste of India’s rich culinary heritage. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook, mastering this classic Murgh Makhani recipe will bring immense satisfaction and a truly delicious meal to your table. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to indulge in one of the world's most beloved curries.
